title: Rabbi David Tawil: Understanding the Amida- "Hazara (Part 2)"

chapters.title: Timing the start of Hazara
chapters.about: When the Hazan should begin the repetition and waiting for others

chapters.title: Minyan requirements for Hazara
chapters.about: How many people must be present and attentive

chapters.title: Birkat Kohanim during Tefila
chapters.about: Performing Birkat Kohanim during the silent Amida

chapters.title: Absence of Hazara in Arvit
chapters.about: The status of Arvit as an optional prayer

chapters.about: Learning Torah or reading Tehillim during the repetition

summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses the laws and customs surrounding the Hazara of the Amida, including when the Hazan should begin the repetition and the importance of the congregation's participation. He addresses the halakhic perspective on waiting for individuals, the requirements for a minyan during the repetition, and the practice of Birkat Kohanim. Additionally, he explores the history of Hazara in Minha and the proper conduct for congregants during the repetition.
questions: Should the Hazan wait for an important person or someone saying Kaddish before starting the Hazara?
How many people are required to be paying attention for the Hazara to begin?
Can a Kohen move from his spot during his silent Amida to perform Birkat Kohanim?
Why is there no Hazara in Arvit?
Is it appropriate to learn Torah or read Tehillim during the Hazara?
